content: Below are detailed explanations of these precautions: Renal Effects Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), including Nabumetone, have been linked to renal papillary necrosis and other forms of kidney damage when used long-term in animal studies. Another type of kidney toxicity associated with NSAIDs occurs in patients with conditions that reduce renal blood flow or blood volume. In such cases, renal prostaglandins play a critical role in maintaining adequate kidney perfusion. When an NSAID is administered, it can lead to a dose-dependent reduction in prostaglandin synthesis, which subsequently decreases renal blood flow. This reduction may result in overt kidney dysfunction or decompensation. Patients most at risk for this adverse effect include those with pre-existing kidney impairment, heart failure, liver dysfunction, those on diuretic therapy, and elderly individuals. If kidney dysfunction occurs, discontinuing the NSAID typically allows the patient to recover to their baseline renal function. Hepatic Function As with other NSAIDs, Nabumetone can cause mild elevations in liver function tests in up to 15% of patients. These abnormalities may either progress, remain stable, or return to normal even with continued therapy. The alanine aminotransferase (ALT, also known as SGPT) test is considered the most sensitive marker for detecting liver dysfunction. Significant elevations in ALT or aspartate aminotransferase (AST, also known as SGOT)—defined as levels three times the upper limit of normal—have been observed in less than 1% of patients during clinical trials of Nabumetone (marketed as RELAFEN). If a patient develops symptoms or signs suggestive of liver dysfunction, or if abnormal liver test results are detected, further evaluation is necessary to determine whether a more severe hepatic reaction is occurring. Severe liver reactions, including jaundice and fatal hepatitis, have been reported with Nabumetone and other NSAIDs, though these events are rare. If liver test abnormalities persist or worsen, or if clinical signs of liver disease (e.g., jaundice, rash, eosinophilia) or systemic symptoms develop, Nabumetone should be discontinued immediately. Fluid Retention and Edema Some patients taking Nabumetone have experienced fluid retention and edema. As with other NSAIDs, Nabumetone should be used with caution in patients who have a history of congestive heart failure, hypertension, or other conditions that predispose them to fluid retention. These patients may be at increased risk of complications related to fluid accumulation. Photosensitivity Nabumetone has been associated with an increased likelihood of photosensitivity reactions based on ultraviolet (UV) light testing.
